sentences.text: As per the FIR registered by first informant Sureshbhai Kalabhai Vankar, he has stated that the present applicants, who are husband and wife and who are NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/14504/2023 ORDER DATED: 18/08/2023 undefined arraigned as accused nos. 2 and 3 in the FIR, lured the first informant for investing the money in their company and thereby first convinced him to invest Rs.3,20,000/- in their company and against that they assured to pay interest at the rate of 1.5% per day by paying Rs.4,500/- towards interest everyday and thereafter the first informant invested Rs.1,20,000/- and was promised to pay interest at the rate of 1% which is Rs.1,050/- every day.
Thereafter, another Rs.5,00,000/- were invested by the first informant, for which he was promised to get Rs.35,00,000/- after 13 months.

Ultimately, the present applicants won the trust of the first informant by paying Rs.40,000/- towards interest over first investment of Rs.3,20,000/- and thereby cheated him to the tune of Rs.9,40,000/- and that is how the FIR is filed.
4. Learned advocate Mr. Chintan Gandhi submitted that the FIR in question is registered after delay of 7 months.
That the applicant wife was the agent of the company and not the owner of the company and accused applicant Sunil Patel was not at all concerned with the company in question.
Learned advocate Mr. Chintan Gandhi submitted that the amount, as alleged, was not given to the present applicants but was invested in the company for which wife Ilaben was working as an agent.
He further submitted that no documentary evidence produced by the first informant to substantiate allegations against the present applicants.

He further submitted NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/14504/2023 ORDER DATED: 18/08/2023 undefined that entire transaction alleged by the first informant had taken place in cash and no amount was paid by cheque or by any electronic means which also questions the genuineness of the FIR.

Learned advocate Mr. Chintan Gandhi also submitted that for the offences alleged the maximum punishment even if the applicants are held guilty of the offences would be of six years and therefore the applicants are required to be considered for anticipatory bail.

5. Learned APP Mr. Utkarsh Sharma vehemently opposed this application and submitted that the investigation is in its preliminary stage and the total amount involved in the entire scam is more than Rs.1,23,00,000/-.

He further submitted that it is alleged that by hatching a conspiracy,
systematically, peoples were duped by making big claim about unrealistic interest and thereby they were cheated.

He further submitted that this being an economic offence and as the total amount is more than one crore, the present applicants may not be considered for anticipatory bail.
6. I have heard learned advocates for the parties and perused the record.
On perusal of the record, I find that the present applicants are instrumental in convincing the first informant to make investment by offering him unrealistic and higher rate of interest.

I have also considered the fact that first informant is not the only person who is duped but as can be NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/14504/2023 ORDER DATED: 18/08/2023 undefined seen from the affidavit filed by the IO before the learned Trial Court that there are number of persons who are also duped by giving similar promise.
The present applicants, along with other co-accused persons, have cheated number of persons and the total amount is more than Rs.1,23,00,000/-.

Therefore, considering the fact that this being an economic offence and it is not only the first informant but there are many other victims also; as also considering the fact that the investigation is in its very early stage, I don't see any reason to consider the case of the present applicants for anticipatory bail, more particularly,

7 . In view of that, present application deserves to be dismissed and accordingly dismissed.
